shared_constraints: Never modify jira_client.py, jira_intake.py, or jira-intake.md: the Jira connector's behaviour must be unchanged at the end of this run.
No shared RUNTIME module between the ADO and Jira connectors - duplication over coupling. A shared TEST asserting cross-provider safety prose is the one sanctioned exception.
stdlib only: no new dependency, no requirements.txt, no third-party import, and no dependency on the Azure CLI.
The read lane stays structurally incapable of a mutating verb: the GET helper takes NO `data` parameter and hardcodes method='GET'.

No URL taken from a response body is ever fetched. Every request URL is composed locally from the validated origin plus a literal path; continuationToken is regex-validated, percent-encoded, and fails closed.
Credentials are read from the environment ONLY, never from argv, and never appear in an artifact, a rendered comment body, or an error message.
Any value that would silently SHRINK the dedupe haystack must raise, never default to empty (missing/empty comment text, missing or non-numeric totalCount, an unmatched continuationToken).
Baseline stays green: all six CI gates, including the coverage floors (per-file and TOTAL 90%).

Every new product module MUST carry a <=5-line `if __name__ == "__main__":` shim. COVERAGE-GATE REGISTRATION RULE: the slice that registers a module in TARGET_FILES / PER_FILE_FLOORS / coverage_omit.txt is the LAST slice that modifies that module, because a floor must be measured on the module's final content. Concretely: ado_intake.py is registered by a3 (no later slice touches it) and ado_client.py is registered by a2 (a2 extends what a1 created) - NOT by a1 and NOT by a5. Set the floor from a fresh local measurement minus >=5 points, rounded down, with the measured figure and date in a trailing comment. Never leave a placeholder like 'XX%' or 'TBD' in PER_FILE_FLOORS.
Command prose must not claim a safety property this repo has not verified; an overstated guarantee on the mutating lane is a defect, not a nit.
HUMAN-ANSWERED SCOPE: the bounded comment-WRITE lane IS in scope this run (slice a2). Every blocking council finding must be implemented, never deferred.

HUMAN-ANSWERED: Azure DevOps SERVICES only. The host allow-list stays a FIXED regex over dev.azure.com and the legacy *.visualstudio.com form, with deliberately NO opt-in extra-hosts variable. A Server/on-prem host must produce a clear refusal naming the supported forms, never a partially working path.

The command's prose must NOT assert marker round-trip fidelity until live evidence is recorded in this run. The operator has agreed to run one live round trip; until then the limit is stated, not claimed away.

WORKTREE CONTAINMENT: edit ONLY files inside your own slice worktree. conventions.md cites repo-root-relative and absolute main-repo paths when it points at existing code - those are READING references. Every WRITE must go to <your worktree>/<same relative path>. Writing to the main checkout contaminates the controller's integration branch.
scope_ceiling: ADO Repos / pull-request support: no ADO lane added to pr_resolver.py, review-pr, or peer-review.
Any generalization or refactor of the Jira connector into a shared provider abstraction.
Azure DevOps Server / on-prem hosts: Azure DevOps Services only (HUMAN-CONFIRMED at intake).

Any ADO write beyond adding one work-item comment: no state transition, no field edit or PATCH, no assignee change, no work-item or child creation, no relation/link edit, no attachment, no comment edit, no comment delete, no reaction.
WIQL / query / board / pipeline surfaces: no searching or listing of work items.
Entra ID / OAuth / service-principal / managed-identity auth flows: PAT only.
Any dependency on the Azure CLI (`az`), including `az devops invoke`.
Changes to the wave loop, dag, run-state, quality gate, or dashboard.

slices.goal: ado_client.py read lane: resolve ONE Azure DevOps work item read-only to the normalized record (org/project/id, HTML-to-text description, acceptance-criteria resolution order, repro steps), plus the fail-closed paginated comment sweep the dedupe gate depends on.

ado_intake.py pure renderer: normalized record + refinement -> pinned-schema intake artifact under .spec-loop-ado/ and the comment bodies it WOULD post, with the org+project+id-scoped in-body dedupe marker and slug-based artifact path.

ado_client.py bounded comment WRITE lane: the sole POST, off by default behind --post, with target-triple verification before credentials, in-batch duplicate rejection, escaped inert bodies, and extraction-based marker dedupe. ALSO registers ado_client.py in the coverage gate (TARGET_FILES, PER_FILE_FLOORS from a fresh local measurement minus >=5, coverage_omit.txt __main__ entry, and the pinned shim block size in test_measure_coverage_manifest.py if it moved) - a2 is the LAST slice to modify ado_client.py, so the floor measured here is final. If a1 already added a placeholder floor, replace it with a real measurement.

The /spec-loop:ado-intake command with the locked allowed-tools and an accurate security boundary, its doctrine test, and the one shared cross-provider test pinning that both connector commands carry the same bounded-write claim set.
